title: Helmet Headset
tagline: A cheap Bluetooth neckband taken apart and rebuilt as a helmet headset
summary: Music, calls and navigation voice in your helmet for about ₹2,650–4,100 instead of a ₹5,000+ communicator, using a cheap Bluetooth neckband's own parts: its board, battery, both speakers and its mic. Its board and buttons go in a slim pod on the outside of the shell on the left (about 59 × 34 mm and 19 mm proud, with room for most neckbands' parts; a round play/call button and a dedicated volume rocker for gloves, sealed, USB-C at the back); its battery goes in its own slim box on the back of the helmet (41 × 32 mm, 12 mm proud), which takes 6 mm off the side pod (or keep it in the pod). Both come off for cleaning: each clips onto a cradle stuck to the helmet with VHB tape (drop it on, slide it down, it clicks), and magnetic pogo connectors in the cradles carry all the wires, so nothing is unplugged. The earbuds' own 10 mm speakers go in printed pucks in the liner's ear pockets; its mic goes on a bendable boom held on the helmet's fixed part, so a modular helmet's chin bar flips up over it. No holes in the helmet: the pod sits along the shell's lower edge, so its wires go straight in under the edge trim (the back box's lead comes down a short grooved channel). General purpose: the helmet's curve is a setting, and the neckband's parts are too (a bigger neckband makes the pod grow).
status: Designed and modelled (v1, checked in CAD, not printed or built yet). Designed first for a modular (flip-up) helmet. Both units clip onto cradles stuck to the helmet. By default the battery goes in a box on the back of the helmet and the side pod holds the board (up to 50 × 12 mm) and the keys; the battery has room up to 35 × 20 × 6 mm (300 mAh class). Most neckbands fit, not all; enter a bigger neckband's sizes and the parts grow.
see_sub: The pod on the left along the lower edge, the battery's box on the back, each on a cradle that stays on the helmet (the helmet is a plain stand-in); inside, the earbuds' speakers in the ear pockets and the neckband's mic on a boom.

gallery.caption: The pod low on the left of a modular helmet (a white stand-in), along the shell's lower edge behind the chin bar's pivot: 19 mm proud with its cradle; the battery in a box on the back
The pod: about 59 × 34 mm; a round play/call button and the volume rocker in a screwed lid, USB-C at the back, its 2 magnetic connectors in its bottom side
Cut through the pod at the volume rocker: one rubber key over 2 switches, its solid middle on a pivot post; the neckband's board below, on the floor
Taking it off: the pod lifted off its cradle, which stays stuck to the helmet with the connectors' other halves (magnetic pogo, 5 pins each) in its ledge. Drop it on, slide it down 6 mm, it clicks
The pod's cradle: 2 dovetail grooves with drop-in windows, a springy tooth at the top (press it to slide the pod off), the connectors in the ledge at the bottom, 3 cable holes facing down
Both units off for cleaning the helmet: the cradles and all the wiring stay on it
The pod's cradle from below: its 3 cables (speakers, mic, battery) leave the ledge facing down, right at the shell's lower edge
The pod on its cradle along the shell's lower edge: the cables go straight in under the edge trim
The back of the helmet: the battery's slim box (41 × 32 mm, 12 mm proud) on its cradle, its lead down a short grooved channel to the lower edge; the side pod low on the left
The back box lifted off its cradle: the TPU cover (snaps on, no screws), the battery in the base, the cradle with its connector; the lead's channel pulled away
Opened up: the lid, the TPU keypad (also the gasket), the switch board, the neckband's board and the 2 connectors in the bottom wall
Inside (the stand-in cut open): the left earbud's speaker in its puck in the ear pocket, the neckband's mic on a boom held low on the fixed shell, reaching into the chin bar
The parts that go inside: a speaker puck holding the earbud's own 10 mm speaker, the boom mount and the mic cup
The back box's channel turned over: the groove for the battery's lead on its underside, thin flanges for the tape

docs.label: README: what goes where, the neckband, the pod, wiring, build order

part_groups.label: The pod and its cradle (outside, left, along the lower edge)
The battery's back box (outside, on the back)

pod_body.name: Pod body
pod_body.what: Holds the neckband's board (and its battery with batt_at = "pod") and the switch board. Its underside sits on the pod's cradle, with 2 short dovetail tongues under it; the 2 magnetic connectors (spring-pin halves) glued in its bottom wall; the USB-C hole at its back end; 4 pillars for M2 heat-set inserts
pod_body.material: PETG or ASA, a light colour if you can. Open side down

pod_lid.name: Pod lid
pod_lid.what: Rolled edges, holes for the play/call button and the volume rocker, a ridge between them; 4 M2 × 6 countersunk screws

rocker_post.name: Rocker pivot post
rocker_post.what: A tiny 3 × 3 mm post glued to the switch board between the volume rocker's 2 switches: the rocker's solid middle rests on it and tips either way

keypad.name: Keypad
keypad.what: One TPU sheet with 2 keys: a round play/call button and a long volume rocker across the pod (raised + on its top end, − on its bottom end); its edge is the seam's gasket, squeezed 0.2 mm by the lid

usb_plug.name: USB-C plug
usb_plug.what: Seals the USB-C socket when you ride; pull it out by its tab (pointing up) to charge

speaker_puck.name: Speaker puck
speaker_puck.what: Holds the earbud's own 10 mm speaker (taken out of its shell) at the middle of the liner's ear pocket, with a small closed space behind it; the back is hollowed. Optional 40 mm helmet speakers fit it too (set the speaker size)

mic_cup.name: Mic cup
mic_cup.what: Holds the neckband's own mic on the end of the boom; a foam windscreen goes over it

boom_mount.name: Boom mount
boom_mount.what: A thin plate that slides between the shell and the liner (or sticks to the shell) low on the left, behind the chin bar; the boom pushes into its socket

headset_assembled.name: Pod, assembled
headset_assembled.what: The pod with its keypad, lid and plug

bb_base.name: Back box: base
bb_base.what: Holds the neckband's battery on the back of the helmet (batt_at = "back"): it sits on its cradle (2 dovetail tongues under it); its connector (the flat half: no live pins when it's off) in its bottom wall; a groove round its walls for the cover's bead

bb_cover.name: Back box: cover
bb_cover.what: Snaps over the base (a bead into its groove) and presses its rim: the seal. No screws

bb_channel.name: Back box: lead channel
bb_channel.what: A short strip with one groove: the battery's lead from the back cradle's bottom side down to the shell's lower edge

pod_cradle.name: Pod cradle
pod_cradle.what: Stays stuck to the shell with VHB tape (its underside curved to it): the pod drops on, slides down 6 mm under the grooves' lips and a springy tooth clicks up behind it. The connectors' flat halves in its ledge (pocket open on top, potted), the cables out of the ledge facing down
pod_cradle.material: PETG / ASA. Top up, supports under it

bb_cradle.name: Back box: cradle
bb_cradle.what: The back box's cradle (batt_at = "back"), stuck to the back of the shell: the same clip-on as the pod's; its connector (the spring-pin half) in its ledge, the battery's lead out of the bottom into the channel
bb_cradle.material: PETG / ASA. Top up, supports under it

params.name: batt_at
params.label: Where the battery goes
choices: in its own box on the back of the helmet (a slimmer side pod)
in the side pod, under the board
params.help: On the back, the side pod is about 6 mm thinner.

params.name: shell_rl
params.label: Shell's radius along the pod (front to back)
params.help: Lay a ruler across the spot: radius = L × L / (8 × gap) + gap / 2.

params.name: shell_rw
params.label: Shell's radius across the pod (up and down)

params.name: run_b
params.label: Back box's channel length
params.help: From the back box's bottom edge straight down to the shell's lower edge.

groups.label: Your neckband (the defaults fit most; enter a bigger one's sizes)

params.name: nb_len
params.label: Board length (along the USB-C)
params.help: The defaults (board 50 × 12, battery 35 × 20 × 6, or a long thin one up to 12 × 50) are room for most neckbands, packed with foam. If yours is bigger, enter its sizes: the pod grows. If the USB-C socket sticks out past the board's end by more than 0.5 mm, add the extra here.

params.name: nb_over
params.label: Tallest part on the board (not the USB-C)

params.name: batt_l
params.label: Battery length
params.help: The neckband's own battery (default room: 35 × 20 × 6, or up to about 50 long if 12 wide or less). The board lies on top of it.

params.name: spk_d
params.label: Speaker diameter (the earbud's own driver)
params.help: The earbuds' own drivers: 10 mm on the Rockerz 255 Pro+. Optional 40 mm helmet speakers: 40 × 5.5.

params.name: mag_l
params.label: Connector face: length
params.help: Along its row of 5 pins, magnets included.

params.name: mag_m
params.label: Spring-pin half: depth behind its face

params.name: mag_f
params.label: Flat half: depth behind its face
